title: Delta's GoCool-150 Goes Big To Enable 150kW Liquid-To-Air Cooling for ASRock Rack's NVIDIA VR NVL72
gist: Delta's GoCool-150, shown at ASRock Rack's Computex 2026 booth alongside a complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, is a 1200kg, 2.3m-tall liquid-to-air CDU that discharges up to 150kW of rack heat into a conventional air-cooled data center — consuming 18kW itself to do so. It exists because AI racks already draw 200kW with 600kW+ planned, while most existing facilities cannot be retrofitted with building-scale liquid loops.

insights.claim: AI server racks already draw 200kW today, with vendors planning 600kW+ racks in the future, driven by high per-chip TDPs combined with rising rack densities.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 3x jump in per-rack draw redefines data center capex per square foot; power and thermal suppliers, not just silicon vendors, capture that spend.
insights.quote: racks that draw 200kW today and plans for 600kW+ racks in the future
insights.locator: A great deal has been made about the power

insights.claim: Powering high-density AI racks is the easier of the two constraints thanks to designs such as 800VDC busbars, leaving heat extraction as the harder unsolved problem.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: If cooling is the binding constraint rather than power delivery, thermal-management vendors sit on the scarcer bottleneck and command better pricing.
insights.quote: Of the two, power is arguably the easier problem to solve, thanks to designs such as 800VDC busbars.
insights.locator: A great deal has been made about the power

insights.claim: Even high-end conventional systems such as the new IBM Z17 mainframes run at much lower power density than a 150kW AI rack, showing how far AI hardware has departed from prior enterprise norms.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Legacy enterprise thermal benchmarks are no longer a useful guide for sizing AI facilities — a repricing risk for older data center assets.

insights.claim: Delta's GoCool-150 is positioned for data centers that want to host direct-liquid-cooled server racks but lack a facility-level liquid-cooling loop.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The addressable market is the entire installed base of air-cooled halls — a large retrofit TAM that does not require new building construction.
insights.locator: Designed to discharge up to 150kW of heat

insights.claim: Data centers originally built around air handlers and hot-air containment cannot be easily retrofitted with building-scale liquid-cooling loops, which is the structural gap the rack-sized heat exchanger fills.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Watch for liquid-to-air CDUs becoming a standard line item in AI colocation deals, since facility-loop retrofits are often economically impossible.
insights.locator: The company is aiming the CDU at data centers

insights.claim: A sufficiently large rack-sized heat exchanger with enough airflow can discharge upwards of 150kW of heat directly into an air-cooled environment, avoiding any facility plumbing change.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Brute-force air rejection sets a practical ceiling on how far liquid cooling can spread without new construction — a gating factor on AI deployment pace.
insights.quote: Build a big enough heat exchanger and run enough air through it, and you can indeed discharge upwards of 150kW of heat into such an environment.
insights.locator: Absent the ability to use those larger heat exchanger setups

insights.claim: The GoCool-150 CDU circulates 225 liters per minute of coolant and is designed to bring that coolant down to 45C.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Flow rate and target temperature are the two specs that determine whether a CDU can pair with a given accelerator rack — a compatibility gate for vendors.
insights.locator: By the numbers, the CDU is designed to circulate

insights.claim: The 45C coolant target matches NVIDIA's Vera Rubin design goal of running off a 45C intake, deliberately traded to make cooling easier and less power-intensive.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA setting a warm-water intake spec cascades into the whole cooling supply chain; vendors that miss the 45C target are designed out.
insights.quote: a major aspect of the systems is to allow them to run off of a 45C intake in order to make them easier to cool and to make that cooling less power-intensive as well
insights.locator: By the numbers, the CDU is designed to circulate

insights.claim: The GoCool-150's 32-fan array moves 17,658 CFM of air, using Delta's in-house PFD2048HT 200mm high-speed fans rated at up to 336 Watts each, 8250 RPM maximum, and up to 81dBA.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Delta building its own fans captures margin in-house and shows the fan itself has become a specialized, high-power component rather than a commodity part.
insights.quote: The cooler’s 32 fan array is capable of moving 17,658 CFM of air
insights.locator: on the back side of the CDU, we find

insights.claim: Both the five coolant pumps and the 32 fans in the GoCool-150 are hot-swappable so failed moving parts can be replaced without any downtime for the CDU or the cooled hardware.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Serviceability without downtime is a requirement when one CDU is a single point of failure for a multi-million-dollar rack — a differentiator versus cheaper units.
insights.locator: at the bottom of the CDU are the coolant pump units

insights.claim: The GoCool-150 CDU alone weighs 1200kg without coolant and stands 2.3 meters tall, and needs 18kW of power itself to discharge 150kW of heat.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 12% parasitic power overhead on cooling plus 1200kg of floor loading are real constraints on retrofit siting and on effective PUE for AI halls.
insights.quote: The cooler needed to discharge 150kW of heat itself needs 18kW.
insights.locator: Overall, the GoCool-150 is a massive box

themes.theme: NVIDIA's go-big strategy and its downstream cost

insights.claim: NVIDIA has made a visible decision to go big with data center hardware to deliver maximum performance, and the result is larger racks, clusters, and coolers across the ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's density choice creates a second wave of spending in rack, cluster and cooling infrastructure that scales with each GPU generation.
insights.quote: NVIDIA has made a very visible decision to go big with its data center hardware to deliver maximum performance, and as a result, we are seeing larger racks, clusters, and coolers.

insights.claim: Liquid cooling obscures how much heat a single Vera Rubin rack generates, and a liquid-to-air exchanger of this scale is the visible measure of what it takes to move that heat with conventional air.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Useful mental model for sizing the thermal build-out: the CDU size is the honest proxy for rack heat that liquid loops hide from the buyer.
insights.quote: The use of liquid cooling somewhat obfuscates just how much heat even a single rack of that hardware can generate.

insights.claim: Liquid-to-air heat exchangers will become increasingly necessary as server racks move to liquid cooling, both for the density it enables and for greater cooling efficiency versus pure air cooling.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A secular demand call on CDU makers — track Delta and peers as a levered play on AI rack deployments in legacy air-cooled facilities.
